title: AegisVox: Factorized Privacy and Clinical Preservation for Long-Form Speech
abstract: arXiv:2610.14643v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Clinical speech reveals identity through both spoken identifiers and voice, yet its pauses, delivery, and speaker roles can also carry useful clinical evidence. Protecting that speech therefore requires more than preserving its words. We present AegisVox, a factorized framework that assigns consistent surrogate voices and edits identifier-bearing turns using document-consistent replacements. Across 390 public simulated or non-patient conversations totaling 63.6 hours, a matched comparison of two speech renderers separates replacement realization from retained identifiers, speaker linkage, and clinical preservation. Text-to-speech rendering realizes 535/601 planned replacements versus 453/601 for the codec-based speech editor. However, similar aggregate clinical preservation conceals more model-labeled contradictions, and conversation-wide speaker scores conceal greater edited-speech linkage under a score-direction sensitivity analysis. F

translated_title: AegisVox：面向长语音的因式分解式隐私保护与临床信息保留
translated_abstract: 临床语音通过口头标识信息和声音特征揭示个人身份，但其停顿、表达方式和说话人角色也可能承载有用的临床证据。因此，保护这类语音不仅仅是保留其文字内容。我们提出了AegisVox，一个因式分解式框架，它为说话人分配一致的替代声音，并使用与文档一致的替换方式编辑包含标识信息的对话轮次。在总计63.6小时的390段公开模拟或非患者对话上，对两种语音渲染器进行的匹配比较将替换实现效果与保留的标识信息、说话人关联性以及临床信息保留分离开来。文本到语音渲染实现了535/601个计划替换，而基于编解码器的语音编辑器实现了453/601个。然而，相似的整体临床保留指标掩盖了更多被模型标记的矛盾，并且在评分方向敏感性分析下，全对话层面的说话人评分掩盖了更大的编辑后语音关联风险。
tldr: AegisVox是一个面向临床长语音的隐私保护框架，通过分配一致的替代声音和编辑包含标识信息的对话内容，在保护隐私的同时保留临床证据，并揭示了聚合评估指标可能掩盖的说话人关联等隐私风险。
